In a July 30 announcement, the US company said investors included pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, and infrastructure and industrial corporate partners\. Commonwealth Fusion, which has attracted the most funding among fusion developers globally, declined to name the investors\. The latest funding raise is among the largest for the global fusion industry, which has been making rapid advances in designs and materials towards commercial fusion power\. Fusion energy seeks to harness the same process that powers the sun to create a clean and almost limitless source of energy and meet growing demand for electricity\. Fusion energy combines lightweight atomic nuclei – typically hydrogen isotopes, deuterium and tritium – to form heavier ones, releasing massive amounts of energy with minimal long-lived radiation and no risk of nuclear meltdowns\. # Commonwealth Fusion Systems Secures $1 Billion for Fusion Reactor Development Commonwealth Fusion Systems \(CFS\) has secured $1 billion in funding to propel its nuclear fusion reactor project, marking a pivotal moment in the pursuit of clean energy solutions\. This investment underscores the increasing confidence in fusion technology as a viable alternative to fossil fuels\. ## Context: The Quest for Fusion Energy Nuclear fusion, the process that powers the sun, has long been considered the holy grail of energy production due to its potential for providing virtually limitless and clean energy\. However, achieving practical fusion has been a daunting challenge, requiring extreme temperatures and pressures\. CFS, founded by scientists from MIT, aims to overcome these hurdles with innovative technologies, notably high-temperature superconductors\. The company’s work is part of a broader global effort to harness fusion energy, with various international projects like the ITER in France showcasing the potential for transformative energy production\. # Devens startup raises another $1 billion to finish its first fusion energy machine - The Boston Globe Commonwealth Fusion Systems, one of the leading startups racing to perfect** **a new clean energy technology, said on Thursday it raised $1 billion in new funding to help complete its first demonstration machine\. The largest venture capital deal in Massachusetts in almost three years, the funding will go towards finishing SPARC, Commonwealth’s proof-of-concept fusion machine in Devens, expected to come online sometime next year, as well as supporting the planning for the company’s first commercial device, dubbed ARC, at a site in Virginia\. “What we used to think was impossible now is feeling more and more inevitable,” cofounder and chief executive Bob Mumgaard said during a Zoom call with reporters\. Mumgaard declined to disclose the identity of the investors or the company’s value based on the new capital infusion\.
